newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nestle shrugs off Greenpeace soy protest.
newsitem.headline: Nestle shrugs off Greenpeace soy protest.

text.p: Nestle Deutschland AG NESG.F on Tuesday said a protest by environmental group Greenpeace over the use of genetically modified soybeans in food products would not change existing company policy.

Greenpeace activists picketed the company headquarters and demanded long-term assurances that Nestle would not use soyoil derived from the modified beans and that it would keep consumers fully informed via labelling.

Nestle spokesman Albrech Koch said he had talked to the campaigners to explain Nestle in Germany was sticking to statements made last October that it would not use soy products derived from the new U.S. crop in response to consumer concern.
The worldwide Swiss Nestle group has said it will use the new products.
Nestle Deutschland would comply with the EU's so-called novel food law, passed on Jan 16, which laid down rules for marketing and labelling of genetically modified food, Koch also said.
Greenpeace sees possible health risks from the new beans, developed by Monsanto Co MTC.N and mixed in with traditional soy.
It said German consumers would be unable to decide if imported Nestle products were free of genetic manipulation and criticised the new labelling law as too lax.
Koch said Nestle Deutschland had replaced its annual soyoil intake with sun oil.
Products using soy derivatives would be labelled as such only if this were mandatory under the novel food law.
Nestle's sales in Germany in 1996 totalled 7.4 billion marks.
